summary:
ASTRA (Astronaut Health Monitoring & Risk Assessment System) is an independent software prototype designed to support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions.

Spaceflight conditions such as radiation exposure, isolation, altered gravity, and confined environments can create challenges for astronaut health. ASTRA addresses this problem through a dashboard that allows users to record health observations, track historical trends, establish personal baselines, and identify notable changes through a transparent, rules-based assessment system.

The application also provides health alerts with suggested actions, mission-condition simulations using synthetic data, and educational resources based on NASA human-spaceflight research.

Built using React, Node.js, Express, and SQLite, ASTRA demonstrates how health observations and mission-context information can be organized into an accessible monitoring platform.

ASTRA is an educational prototype, not a medical diagnostic tool or a NASA-developed or NASA-endorsed system. Its simulated data and assessment rules are not clinically validated.
details:
Project Details – ASTRA

1. What does ASTRA do?

ASTRA (Astronaut Health Monitoring & Risk Assessment System) is an independent software prototype designed to support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions.

Space missions expose astronauts to several challenges, including space radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, distance from Earth, and hostile environments. These conditions can contribute to health-related challenges involving cardiovascular health, bone health, sleep, nutrition, and behavioral well-being.

ASTRA addresses the need to organize and monitor health observations over time through an accessible digital platform.

2. How does it work?

ASTRA provides an integrated health-monitoring dashboard with several interconnected modules:

  • Dashboard: Provides an overview of the health-monitoring system and mission information.
  • Health Records: Allows users to enter and manage observations such as heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body temperature, glucose, sleep duration, mood, stress level, and symptoms.
  • Health History and Visualizations: Stores observations and displays historical trends through interactive charts, making changes easier to review.
  • Personal Baseline and Health Analysis: Calculates individual reference averages from previous health records and compares newer observations against those baselines to identify notable changes.
  • Health Alerts and Guidance: Highlights notable changes and provides understandable messages with suggested follow-up actions.
  • Mission Profile: Displays a demonstration mission overview and mission information.
  • Mission Simulation: Provides five synthetic scenarios: nominal conditions, elevated radiation exposure, extended isolation, altered gravity, and combined mission challenges.
  • NASA Research: Provides educational resources about spaceflight hazards and human health research.

The system uses a transparent, rules-based assessment engine rather than relying on an external AI service.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA aims to make astronaut health observations more organized, accessible, and understandable.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Supporting consistent tracking of health observations.
  • Helping users review changes over time instead of looking at isolated measurements.
  • Providing individual reference baselines for comparison.
  • Highlighting observations that may require further attention.
  • Connecting mission-environment challenges with educational health information.
  • Offering a simulation environment to explore different spaceflight scenarios.

The intended impact is to demonstrate how a structured digital monitoring platform could support health awareness and help organize information for further review by appropriate medical and mission personnel.

4. Technology Used

ASTRA was developed using accessible, open-source technologies:

Frontend:

  • React.js
  • Vite
  • JavaScript
  • CSS
  • Recharts for health visualizations
  • Lucide React for interface icons

Backend:

  • Node.js
  • Express.js
  • REST APIs

Database:

  • SQLite
  • better-sqlite3

Development Tools:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub

The prototype runs as a web application and does not require dedicated hardware or paid AI APIs.

5. What makes ASTRA creative?

ASTRA brings together health record management, personal baseline comparison, trend visualization, alert generation, mission simulation, and NASA human-spaceflight research within one platform.

An important aspect of its approach is the use of individual historical observations as reference points rather than depending exclusively on generic comparison values.

The mission simulation module also provides an interactive way to explore synthetic mission conditions without modifying actual health records. This keeps demonstration scenarios separate from stored observations.

6. Factors Considered During Development

The development focused on:

  • Transparency: Assessment rules and notable changes are understandable rather than hidden behind a black-box model.
  • Privacy: The prototype uses a local SQLite database during development and does not require external health-data transmission.
  • Accessibility: A clear dashboard, organized navigation, visual charts, and responsive layouts make information easier to explore.
  • Reliability: Input validation, historical record management, and API error handling help maintain data consistency.
  • Safety: Simulated observations are clearly identified as synthetic, and assessment rules are illustrative rather than clinically validated.
  • Cost-effectiveness: The project uses open-source technologies and avoids paid external AI services.

7. Future Scope

Future development could include integration with validated astronaut health-monitoring devices, secure data synchronization, offline-first capabilities, expanded mission-environment monitoring, and assessment methods validated by qualified medical professionals.

Conclusion

ASTRA demonstrates a practical software-based approach to organizing astronaut health observations and exploring health-monitoring concepts for long-duration space missions. By combining personal baselines, historical trends, understandable alerts, mission simulations, and educational research, ASTRA aims to contribute to the broader goal of supporting human health and well-being beyond Earth.

ASTRA is an independent educational prototype. It is not developed, approved, or endorsed by NASA, is not a medical diagnostic tool, and does not replace professional medical assessment or official mission health protocols.
